empathy.justification: The assistant never apologizes emptily, which is good. It also never acknowledges the customer's frustration, even after the customer says they were stuck in a support loop and later says 'That's not helpful.' It does mention the deadline ('given your deadline'), but the tone stays transactional. Turn 1 opens with a flat refusal.
quotes: I can't reverse that charge — I'm an AI assistant with no access to billing systems
What to do right now (given your deadline):
empathy.improvement: Add one brief, sincere line acknowledging the support loop and the pressure of the bill due tomorrow before giving next steps. Avoid opening with a blunt refusal.

resolution_quality.justification: The assistant can't access billing systems and says so honestly. Within that limit it gives a usable path: escalate to the bank, contact the merchant, and use an email template that reuses the transaction IDs the customer already has, so they don't redo work. Weaknesses: Turn 1 suggests contacting support, which the customer had already tried. Turn 2 repeats generic channels. The assistant never asks for the company name directly as a way to gather the key missing information. It also doesn't explain how to escalate if the merchant ignores the template.
quotes: Most can issue a provisional credit quickly, which would protect your bill due tomorrow.
Please reverse the duplicate charge immediately. This is time-sensitive
resolution_quality.improvement: Ask for the company name directly in the first turn. Add escalation steps after sending the template, such as a follow-up timeline and when to fall back to a bank dispute.

policy_clarity.justification: The assistant invents no merchant policy and is honest about its own limits. However, it gives no realistic timelines: refunds typically take 3-10 business days to post, and an issued refund may not clear before tomorrow. It doesn't explain the difference between a pending authorization and a posted charge. It says 'quickly' about provisional credit without qualification.
quotes: Most can issue a provisional credit quickly
I can't guarantee I'll have a current, verified number.
policy_clarity.improvement: Say plainly that merchant refunds often take several business days to post, so even a successful request may not clear by tomorrow. Note that a duplicate pending charge may drop off on its own.

overall_impression: Honest and practical, and the final template is useful. However, the responses are emotionally flat, partly repeat advice the customer had already ruled out, and omit realistic refund timelines that matter for the next-day deadline.
